## Data Download Instructions

### Dataset 1 — World Happiness Report (Problem 1)

1. Go to **[https://www.worldhappiness.report/data-sharing/](https://www.worldhappiness.report/data-sharing/)**

2. Click "Download data for Figure 2.1" — this will download an Excel file (`.xlsx`)

3. Place the downloaded file in the **same folder** as this `.Rmd`

4. Update the filename (and file path if necessary) in the code chunk below to match what you downloaded

```{r load-happiness}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)

happy <- read_excel("data/WHR26_Data_Figure_2.1.xlsx")

# Keep only the most recent observation per country
happy <- happy %>%
  group_by(`Country name`) %>%
  slice_max(Year, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(country   = `Country name`,
         year      = Year,
         happiness = `Life evaluation (3-year average)`,
         log_gdp   = `Explained by: Log GDP per capita`) %>%
  drop_na(happiness, log_gdp)
```

### Dataset 2 — NOAA Global Surface Temperature Anomalies (Problem 2)

1. Go to **[https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/climate-at-a-glance/global/time-series](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/climate-at-a-glance/global/time-series)**

2. Set the following options:
   - **Region:** Global
   - **Surface:** Land and Ocean
   - **Parameter:** Average Temperature Departure
   - **Time Scale:** 12-Month
   - **Filter:** No Filter
   - **Month:** All Months
   - **Start Year:** 1960 · **End Year:** 2023

3. Click **"Plot"**, then click **"Download: CSV"**

4. Place the downloaded file in the **same folder** as this `.Rmd`

5. Update the filename (and file path if necessary) in the code chunk below to match what you downloaded

```{r load-temp}
temp_raw <- read.csv("data/NOAA.csv", skip = 4)
names(temp_raw) <- c("year", "anomaly")

# Center year at 1960 so the intercept has a meaningful interpretation
temp <- temp_raw %>%
  mutate(year_c = year - 1960)
```
